title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The UK government has responded to the 2020 Committee report on Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards, outlining a strategy to strengthen AI governance, transparency, and accountability across public services. It commits to creating clear standards, promoting responsible AI use, and working with stakeholders to build public trust and ensure equitable outcomes.

title: EM on EU Regulation 2024/1689 on Artificial Intelligence
description: The government's summary of an EU regulation laying down harmonised rules on artificial intelligence and amending several Regulations and Directives.
summary: Europe’s new EU Regulation 2024/1689 establishes uniform rules for the design, deployment, and supervision of artificial intelligence across the bloc, prioritising safety, transparency, and accountability. The government explains how this regulation revises existing laws—such as directives on data protection and cybersecurity—to create a harmonised legal framework that governs AI technologies.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual is outlining how artificial intelligence can be used safely and fairly in England’s qualifications system, aiming to preserve exam integrity and student confidence. The policy will set clear rules, monitor AI tools, and work with educators and exam bodies to keep assessment standards high and transparent.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: The document examines how copyrighted works are used in training and deploying AI systems, assessing the legal and ethical implications of these practices. It evaluates the impact on creators, society, and the AI industry, offering recommendations to balance intellectual property rights with technological advancement.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The UK government has responded to the House of Lords Select Committee’s report “AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency” by outlining a plan to strengthen AI governance, increase investment in research and innovation, and ensure ethical and transparent use of AI technologies. It highlights the need for clear regulations, collaboration with industry and academia, and a national strategy to keep the UK competitive while safeguarding public interests.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: This document explains the purpose, scope, and duties of a committee that will study how artificial intelligence intersects with public standards and provides a set of frequently asked questions to help stakeholders understand the review process. It outlines the committee’s objectives, meeting structure, participants, and key topics to be examined.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: CSPL has provided written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee’s inquiry into the governance of Artificial Intelligence. Their submission outlines the organization’s concerns and offers recommendations for creating transparent, accountable, and ethical AI systems.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: This policy looks at how AI changes the rules for medical products and how those rules must adapt. It also explains how to apply the principles laid out in the AI White Paper to make sure medical AI is safe and trustworthy.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: This policy outlines how the defense organization plans to lead in AI, aiming to be the most effective, efficient, trusted, and influential for its size. It sets strategies and priorities to achieve that goal.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The Transport Artificial Intelligence Action Plan explains how the Department for Transport will partner with the transport sector to take advantage of AI’s benefits while carefully managing its risks. It lays out clear steps and safeguards for responsibly integrating AI into transport systems.
